thread:
Maya: FYI we've seen a growing tail on cold-starts for GPU pods in eu-west over the last week — 15s median -> 45s P95. Looks correlated with older instance image versions and longer NVPeer attach times.
Ryan: ugh. any correlation with preemptible churn or is this pure image/kernel noise?
Maya: mostly image/kernel. Preemptible churn did spike but these samples are from stable reserved pools. I ran a quick sample: `strace` shows long `mmap` on /dev/nvidia0 during container init.
Oliver: could be driver init or CUDA context warmup. We saw similar once when the runtime switched minor driver version and contexts had to relocate. Do we have histogram by instance age?
Maya: yes — run attached: `spinup_age_hist.csv` shows P95 spinup grows with instance age bucket >60 days. Might be memory fragmentation at the vendor kernel layer.
Sophie: If spinups shift P95 from 15s->45s that kills short-latency SLA for interactive chat. We can either overprovision warm pool or accept higher headroom. Cost+impact?
Ryan: cost calc quick: keeping a 10% warm pool in eu-west adds ~0.12 GPU-hrs/user-month for our median workload -> ~$3k/mo. But reduces tail-related retries and user latency incidents.
Maya: also noticed that batching windows widen because some nodes take longer to bootstrap their KV cache, so tokens/sec dips for ~30s after scale-up events. That amplifies latency beyond the single-request spinup.
Oliver: two mitigation proposals: 1) proactive rolling of old instance images (force reimage <45d age), 2) lightweight warm pool that boots only the driver+runtime and awaits container. 1 is ops-heavy but cheap; 2 has higher infra cost but faster reaction.
Sophie: both good. Also think about predictive spinup: use traffic signal (12-min moving average of qps) to pre-warm an extra N nodes before expected shoulder. That avoids cold starts during known spikes.
Maya: I ran a 24h sim with our traffic traces + predicted spinup (lead time 60s) and it trimmed tail by 70% for the same 10% warm pool cost. Will share sim graph later.
Ryan: nice. We should also add a short-term patch: if NVPeer attach takes >10s, treat node as degraded and route new requests to other zones (fast-failover). Can we implement a runtime-level healthcheck?
Oliver: yep — runtime expose `nv_attach_latency_ms` gauge; we can add alert and route rule in smart-router.
infra-bot: deploy candidate for `smart-router/eviction-fallback` created in staging (#1208). CI green. :rocket:
Sophie: next steps: (a) Maya share sim + csv, (b) Ryan get cost delta for 5/10/15% warm pools across eu-west/us-west, (c) Oliver prototype nv_attach healthcheck + route rule. I'll own rollout plan and doc.
Maya: sharing files now: https://redwood.internal/sim/2234500000-spinup-sim.png and `spinup_age_hist.csv` attached. Quick note: logs show kernel OOM events in a small subset — might be compounding factor.
Ryan: flagged for infra-sre to triage kernel OOMs separately.
Oliver: I'll sketch a tiny config for router fallback and test in canary later today.
Sophie: cool. If we can cut P95 by 30-40% with config+circuit-breaker we avoid full fleet reimages for now. thanks all. :thumbsup:
